name: Assyrian Neo-Aramaic
catalog_quote: In Assyrian, stress is expiratory and normally is placed on the penultimate. It is not shifted in verb suffixation (i.e. is goes to the newly formed penultimate). Stress often affects the quality and length of vowels; it may cause the ommission of vowels and, at times, of entire syllables. (Tsereteli 1978)

audit.reasoning: Quote check: Maclean 1895 sect. 8 p.13 statement found verbatim in the held scanned text; Stoddard 1855:20 corroboration fetched sources and confirmed; Noeldeke 1868 sect. 30 fetched sources and agrees (second-hand from Stoddard); open-access NENA volumes we hold and Coghill 2020 give only family-level 'penultimate unless marked' notes. Every source seen agrees that default word stress is penultimate, so the rule string '10 010 0010...' is not in doubt and nothing suggests a recode of the position. The weakness is vintage and kind: the classification rests on a database entry (StressTyp2 < Tsereteli 1978, unverified) checked against an 1895 missionary reference grammar, while a 2016 four-volume reference grammar of the same dialect (Khan, Urmi) and a 1988 phonology monograph (Odisho) exist and are not held. Maclean's own sect. 8 (5)-(7) and Stoddard already record affix/enclitic-conditioned antepenult and some oxy
